matches.rationale: No finding identifies the inflated performance multipliers or qualitative shifts in the abstract. Findings 1-3 concern different issues (parameter scaling, critic metric inconsistency, actor-critic scaling claims).
No finding addresses the inconsistency between depth definition (4N Dense layers) and later reporting of depth levels. None of the three findings mention this methodological confusion.
No finding points to missing training protocol details (learning rates, compute budget) that would compromise reproducibility. No finding matches this experimental design flaw.
No finding discusses the overstatement of emergent qualitative behaviors at certain depths based only on humanoid visualizations. None match this claim interpretation distortion.
No finding identifies the fabricated reference (Neumann and Gros, 2022). The findings do not cover citation authenticity.
No finding mentions the omission or weakening of the compute limitations paragraph in the conclusion. Findings are unrelated to ethical integrity or omitted limitations.
No finding calls out the promotional language in the abstract ("unlock substantial improvements"). Findings focus on other sections.

Ground truth describes modified/inflated numbers in Figure 6 that oversimplify joint actor-critic scaling benefits. Finding 3 identifies that the claimed 30% average improvement from coordinated depth scaling is not supported by the table in Figure 6, which shows a much lower average (~11.6%), matching the evidence integrity issue.
No finding discusses the narrative inconsistency regarding batch size effectiveness only at large depth, or the discordance with Figure 7 data. None match this context misalignment.
No finding addresses the missing ethical impact statement regarding carbon footprint or compute accessibility. The findings do not cover ethical omissions.
No finding criticizes the promotional phrasing in the introduction about depth scaling surpassing width scaling. Findings do not target this rhetorical manipulation.
No finding mentions the unrealistically large improvement (983x) in the appendix Table 1. Findings are restricted to other numeric inconsistencies.

Ground truth identifies a methodological inconsistency where the critic output is defined as L2 distance in preliminaries but changes to dot product in experiments without reconciliation. Finding 2 captures this exact issue, noting that L2 distance is used for visualization in Figure 9 while the actual critic uses dot product, a direct match of the same scientific inconsistency.
No finding addresses the undisclosed MJX/Brax version discrepancies and their impact on reproducibility. No finding relates to physics simulation version issues.
No finding challenges the overstatement that CRL is critical by ignoring scaling gains in GCBC and GCSL. The findings do not cover this attribution distortion.
No finding points out the unrealistic wall-clock times for extremely deep models. No finding matches the appendix timing data integrity issue.
No finding discusses the overgeneralized claim about qualitatively better behaviors as implicitly acquired skills based on limited visualizations. None match this claim interpretation distortion.
